An active-duty U.S. Air Force major who was arrested by U.S. Capitol Police yesterday after conducting a protest on the Capitol steps while in uniform calling for the impeachment of President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance is now under investigation by the Pentagon. Service members are prohibited from participating in partisan political activities while in uniform and are subject to additional restrictions under the Uniform Code of Military Justice regarding public statements about senior government officials. Without identifying the officer, the office of Air Force Secretary Troy Meink acknowledged reports of the incident, stating that an investigation "will proceed unimpeded." The Department of the Air Force also reiterated that all personnel are expected to comply with laws, regulations, and policies governing conduct and the wear of the uniform.

The U.S. Coast Guard has released additional details on the June 22 MH-60T "Jayhawk" helicopter crash on Harbor Mountain near Sitka, Alaska. All four crew members sustained only minor injuries and were released from the local hospital the same day. While the cause of the crash remains under investigation, a newly released photo from U.S. Coast Guard District Arctic shows the aircraft sustained extensive damage. Beginning next week, the Alaska Army National Guard's Downed Aircraft Recovery Team will begin recovery operations at the crash site, which remains closed to the public due to hazardous conditions. In the meantime, Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak continues supporting search & rescue coverage while Air Station Sitka works toward resuming flight operations next week. Source: news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases…

The Wall Street Journal reports the Pentagon was prepared to announce additional reductions to the U.S. military presence in Europe beyond previously canceled and withdrawn deployments, but the proposal was halted by senior White House officials. Instead, the administration opted to proceed with the six-month U.S. force posture review announced by Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth at last month's NATO defense ministers' meeting. If accurate, the report suggests the administration remains divided over the pace and scope of any future troop reductions in Europe. At the same time, it reinforces the Pentagon's broader strategy of shifting greater responsibility for Europe's conventional defense to NATO allies while freeing U.S. forces for higher-priority theaters, particularly the Indo-Pacific. Source: wsj.com/politics/national-se…

Educação e saúde protagonistas em Juazeiro do Norte (CE). Na última agenda desta quinta, entregamos 40 novos ônibus do Caminho da Escola para municípios cearenses. O programa garante que nossos jovens cheguem à sala de aula com segurança e conforto. Desde 2023, já são 215 veículos destinados ao estado. Em todo o país, o projeto envolve 2,5 mil ônibus escolares, com investimento de R$ 1,2 bilhão. Adicionalmente, entregamos 29 consultórios odontológicos móveis. As unidades realizam procedimentos clínicos, ações de prevenção e promoção da saúde bucal e fortalecem a Atenção Primária à Saúde. Entregamos ainda 19 veículos para transporte de pacientes para consultas, exames e tratamentos. Garantir oportunidades iguais de educação para todos, cuidar da saúde bucal e garantir que a população do interior e das áreas rurais tenha atendimento médico de qualidade é garantir dignidade e cidadania ao povo brasileiro. 📷 @ricardostuckert

Le solicito a los medios públicos la transmisión de las reuniones de empalme de gobierno Voces (@vocesco) #Voces | El presidente Gustavo Petro propuso que el proceso de empalme entre su gobierno y la administración entrante de Abelardo de la Espriella sea transmitido por televisión, con el objetivo de que los colombianos puedan conocer de primera mano cómo avanza la entrega del Estado y el intercambio de información entre ambos equipos. La propuesta fue planteada en medio de las tensiones que han rodeado el inicio de la transición presidencial. Según el mandatario, la transmisión permitiría garantizar mayor transparencia y evitar especulaciones sobre el contenido de las reuniones, los informes de las entidades y las decisiones adoptadas durante el proceso de empalme. El planteamiento surge luego de que el equipo del presidente electo denunciara presuntas irregularidades en los últimos días de la administración Petro, entre ellas nombramientos y decisiones administrativas que, según la nueva administración, deberían ser revisadas durante el empalme. Por su parte, el Gobierno ha reiterado que entregará toda la información conforme a los procedimientos establecidos por la ley. De acuerdo con el cronograma definido para la transición, el proceso contempla la instalación de mesas sectoriales en las diferentes entidades del Estado, la socialización de informes de gestión y la elaboración de las actas finales que deberán entregarse antes de la posesión del nuevo gobierno. Incluso, el protocolo prevé una reunión entre el presidente saliente y el presidente electo, aunque hasta el momento no se ha confirmado una fecha para ese encuentro. La iniciativa de televisar el empalme aún no ha sido aceptada oficialmente por el equipo de Abelardo de la Espriella. Sin embargo, la propuesta se suma a las discusiones sobre cómo garantizar una transición transparente en medio de un ambiente político marcado por la polarización y los cuestionamientos entre el Gobierno saliente y la administración entrante. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/vocesco/status/2072789949921833396#m

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, and Prof. K. V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, participated in a panel discussion on "Data, Statistics and India's Growth Agenda", held as part of "Swarna Andhra @ 2047: Economic Intelligence for Governance", a two-day capacity-building programme organised by the Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh. The panel was moderated by Shri Suresh Goyal, Director General, NCAER, and featured Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India; and Prof. S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman, EAC-PM, as fellow panellists. Dr. Balasubramaniam emphasised that data must serve as a foundation for dignity in governance, making visible those often overlooked in averages, including informal workers and tribal communities. He noted that while India already has rich individual-level data, the priority now is to harmonise datasets across ministries, break institutional silos, and use evidence to strengthen social development and citizen capability. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat, he stressed that better decisions depend on engaging with what the data truly reveals and viewing citizens as active participants in the development journey. The programme's broader context was set by Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu, whose address emphasised translating the State's growth vision into measurable, mission-mode outcomes, integrating datasets across departments and geographies, and pursuing growth that is sustainable and inclusive. @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp @drrbalu

When it comes to protecting the lives and livelihoods of our people, there is no Government or Opposition only Sri Lanka. Today, at the National Council for Disaster Management chaired by H.E the President, I shared a strategic science-backed proposal to help Sri Lanka prepare for the anticipated climate risks of 2026–27. My message was simple; we cannot afford to wait for disaster to strike we must act. By strengthening early warning systems, safeguarding our food and water security, and planning together as a nation, we can create greater resilience against climate change. NewsWire 🇱🇰 (@NewsWireLK) Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed a series of measures to strengthen Sri Lanka’s climate resilience and disaster preparedness, warning that the country should act now to prepare for the anticipated impacts of the 2026-2027 El Niño cycle. Speaking at the National Council for Disaster Management, chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Premadasa said climate security has become a national priority that requires a united, science-based response beyond political differences. Citing global scientific assessments, Premadasa warned that the developing El Niño could be among the strongest in recent decades, bringing prolonged droughts followed by severe flooding. He said Sri Lanka should move away from responding to disasters after they occur and instead adopt an anticipatory governance model based on scientific forecasting, risk assessments and early preparedness. Among his key proposals was making climate resilience a whole-of-government responsibility involving institutions responsible for agriculture, water resources, energy, health, finance, defence, provincial administration and local government. Premadasa also called for integrated reservoir management to improve water security, expansion of climate-smart agriculture to strengthen food security, and the modernisation of early warning systems through impact-based forecasting that provides communities with more actionable information before disasters strike. He further proposed strengthening disaster risk financing, improving preparedness for heatwaves and public health emergencies, enhancing the resilience of critical infrastructure, and establishing a National Climate Risk and Disaster Intelligence Centre to support evidence-based decision-making across Government. Premadasa said Sri Lanka should also draw lessons from countries such as India and Australia, which have strengthened climate forecasting, agricultural contingency planning and broader resilience initiatives in response to growing climate risks. Looking beyond the immediate El Niño threat, he proposed the preparation of a Presidential White Paper on National Climate Resilience and Disaster Preparedness to establish a long-term policy framework that would guide future governments. He stressed that climate resilience cannot be achieved by the Government alone and requires the participation of Parliament, provincial and local authorities, the scientific community, universities, the private sector, civil society, international development partners and local communities. Premadasa added that protecting the lives and livelihoods of Sri Lankans must remain a shared national responsibility. ⭕️ German federal prosecutors indicted a 50-year-old Ukrainian man identified as Serhii K over the 2022 explosions that destroyed the Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipelines linking Russia to Europe. Prosecutors allege he helped coordinate a team that used a sailing yacht to plant explosives near Denmark’s Bornholm Island, serving as the operation’s on-board coordinator rather than as a diver or bomb expert. Serhii K, previously identified as Serhii Kuznietsov after his 2025 arrest in Italy and extradition to Germany, has denied involvement and says he was serving in Ukraine’s armed forces at the time, while the Ukrainian government has also continued to deny involvement in the attack which severed a critical export corridor for Russian natural gas. Dr Nika Soon-Shiong said she was removed from the board of the Committee to Protect Journalists after challenging a decision she feared would see Palestinians broadly excluded from journalist death tolls. She told MEE “there are bad faith attacks” on the organisation seeking to lobby against Palestinians’ inclusion. Last week, the CPJ said it was reviewing its documentation of journalists killed during the Israel-Gaza War. 20 Palestinians were delisted after militant groups published obituaries identifying them as members. International law protects the civilian status of journalists working for state or militant groups on the condition they are not directly involved in combat. The CPJ’s board has since voted against changes to their definition of journalist, in a move welcomed by Soon-Shiong. The press freedom group rejected claims it had sought to exclude particular groups, and flatly denied that political influence played a role in triggering the review. Video

One week after the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela, which have claimed close to 2,000 lives and left many more dead, injured, displaced, or still unaccounted for, we mourn with the families and communities affected by this tragedy. As humanitarian needs continue to grow, it is essential that assistance reaches all those in need in a timely, transparent, and non-discriminatory manner. Venezuelan authorities should facilitate, rather than hinder, the delivery of aid and access to affected communities. Independent civil society organizations can play a vital role in monitoring relief efforts, identifying gaps in assistance, and helping ensure accountability. They should be granted access to transparent information and data necessary to assess needs, monitor the response, and verify official statistics. Authorities should also provide information on the whereabouts and conditions of all political prisoners and immediately release those arbitrarily detained. At this critical moment, transparency, accountability, and respect for humanitarian principles are indispensable to an effective response and to protecting the rights of all those affected. 🚨Ukraine: last night, the Russian military carried out a massive attack on Kyiv. Official reports so far confirm 20 deaths and at least 86 wounded. Among the targets was an ambulance station, where three paramedics and three driver-technicians were injured. The attack also damaged a hotel and residential buildings; people who were sleeping were trapped under the rubble. The city’s healthcare system was overwhelmed, with reports that 110 ambulance crews were working simultaneously to respond to emergencies. “We start a new day yet again with shock and horror - the idea that ambulance and emergency-response teams have to dig people out from the remains of destroyed residential blocks – and save the lives of their own colleagues who have been targeted,” says Robin Meldrum, Country Director for MSF in Ukraine. We once again emphasise that medical workers and healthcare facilities throughout Ukraine remain unprotected, working under constant threat and on the verge of resource depletion. We condemn the attacks by Russian forces, which endanger not only people but also their ability to receive medical care after being wounded.

TeamPCP has also engaged in extortion and collaboration with cyber actors from other threat actor groups, publishing victim names on a public leak site and threatening to release stolen data. My meeting with 🇹🇷 Health Minister Prof Dr Kemal Memişoğlu was above all an opportunity to say thank you: for Türkiye’s leadership, hospitality and partnership throughout the WHO Ministerial Conference on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management. Together, our teams at Türkiye’s Ministry of Health and WHO/Europe turned months of preparation into a tangible result: the Istanbul Outcome Statement on protecting health in earthquakes. For me, these 2 days showed the WHO I believe in: convening countries, learning from real experience, and helping shape shared standards and norms for stronger earthquake emergency management. I thanked Türkiye for making health a dedicated part of the #COP31 agenda in Antalya and reaffirmed WHO/Europe’s readiness to support cooperation on climate and health. We also discussed our partnership on Anatolian medicine and how Türkiye’s experience can be shared more widely, with a focus on evidence, safety, quality and people-centred care.

Preparations for the 50th anniversary of the Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care were a key focus of my exchange with Dr Akmaral Alnazarova, Kazakhstan’s Minister of Health. Meeting on the margins of the WHO Ministerial Conference in Istanbul on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management, we also explored how the Istanbul Outcome Statement can support practical cooperation through the network of Emergency Medical Teams under the Organization of Turkic States. I welcomed Kazakhstan’s interest in WHO classification of Emergency Medical Teams, and discussed the value of a Joint External Evaluation to assess capacities to prevent, detect and respond to public health threats, and to guide future investments in health security.

Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he says, "Somebody is saying that fuel mileage is going to drop. It is now well established that ethanol is even used in racing cars. Acceleration improves. What is that called? Knocking? Knocking also improves. Mileage? Yes, it may drop a little. But it may drop slightly due to various factors... Secondly, after consulting all stakeholders, including SIAM and ARAI, we have reached this stage. Then someone says, 'Your insurance will no longer cover this'. Insurance companies have already clarified that there is no such issue. But who benefits from spreading this false narrative? I am not going to make any accusations, but one thing should be very clear. There is enough space in India's growing consumer market for all technologies to coexist. There is room for electric vehicles, biofuel blended vehicles, and we are currently only at 20 per cent ethanol blending. If we move from 20 per cent to 25 per cent, it will happen only after all the necessary tests have been completed. There is also enough space for hybrid vehicles and CNG vehicles..." One week after the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela, which have claimed close to 2,000 lives and left many more dead, injured, displaced, or still unaccounted for, we mourn with the families and communities affected by this tragedy. As humanitarian needs continue to grow, it is essential that assistance reaches all those in need in a timely, transparent, and non-discriminatory manner. Venezuelan authorities should facilitate, rather than hinder, the delivery of aid and access to affected communities. Independent civil society organizations can play a vital role in monitoring relief efforts, identifying gaps in assistance, and helping ensure accountability. They should be granted access to transparent information and data necessary to assess needs, monitor the response, and verify official statistics. Authorities should also provide information on the whereabouts and conditions of all political prisoners and immediately release those arbitrarily detained. At this critical moment, transparency, accountability, and respect for humanitarian principles are indispensable to an effective response and to protecting the rights of all those affected. LabPazVe (@LabPazVe) Laboratorio de Paz. A 1 semana de los terremotos del 24.06.2026. Los terremotos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026 han dejado una profunda huella de dolor, pérdidas humanas, personas heridas, familias damnificadas, viviendas destruidas o severamente afectadas, comunidades enteras en situación de vulnerabilidad y una enorme incertidumbre para millones de personas dentro y fuera del país. A una semana del trágico evento, el Laboratorio de Paz reafirma su profundo respeto y solidaridad con las víctimas fatales, sus familiares, las personas heridas, quienes han perdido sus hogares, sus pertenencias, sus medios de vida, y con todas las comunidades afectadas en el país. Acompañamos el dolor de quienes hoy aún esperan noticias de sus seres queridos y reconocemos la angustia de miles de familias que permanecen fuera de sus viviendas esperando noticias de sus familiares. A pesar del tiempo transcurrido desde los sismos, es indispensable que las labores de búsqueda, rescate y recuperación continúen con todos los recursos disponibles. Mientras exista la posibilidad de encontrar personas con vida, no podemos perder la esperanza. Cada minuto cuenta, cada esfuerzo importa y cada vida debe ser buscada con la máxima diligencia, coordinación y humanidad. La magnitud de esta tragedia exige que se mantenga el despliegue de equipos especializados, asistencia internacional, apoyo técnico y presencia humanitaria en las zonas más afectadas. Nuevamente insistimos en la obligación de primacía de la dignidad para atender la crisis, claridad, transparencia y responsabilidad en el manejo de la información sobre personas fallecidas, heridas, desaparecidas, rescatadas y damnificadas. Las familias tienen derecho a saber. El país tiene derecho a información pública, verificable, oportuna y desagregada. La opacidad y limitaciones al derecho a la información no protege a nadie; aumenta la angustia, dificulta la asistencia, obstaculiza la identificación de necesidades y debilita aún más la confianza en la respuesta. La atención a quienes lo perdieron todo debe ser eficaz, rápida, digna y sin discriminación. Las personas damnificadas necesitan refugios seguros, agua, alimentos, atención médica, apoyo psicosocial, información clara, protección frente a abusos, soluciones habitacionales sostenibles rápidas. La emergencia debe ser atendida con enfoque de derechos humanos, transparencia en el uso de los recursos y participación de la sociedad y de las comunidades afectadas. No pueden repetirse experiencias pasadas, respuestas improvisadas o asistencias temporales sin seguimiento. Esta emergencia debe ser asumida con memoria, responsabilidad y aprendizaje. La reconstrucción no puede convertirse en una nueva fuente de exclusión, abandono, corrupción o revictimización. Destacamos la labor fundamental de periodistas, comunicadores y trabajadores de la prensa que han estado cubriendo la emergencia desde el primer momento, muchas veces en condiciones precarias, con recursos propios y bajo restricciones. Su trabajo es indispensable para documentar lo ocurrido, orientar a la ciudadanía, visibilizar necesidades, verificar información, acompañar a las víctimas y exigir respuestas Reconocemos con profundo orgullo la fortaleza, la capacidad solidaria y la dignidad del pueblo venezolano. En medio del dolor, millones de personas han salido de forma independiente, autónoma y libre a ayudar a vecinos, a remover escombros, a crear centros de acopio, atender la salud sin descanso, a informar sin sesgos, a arriesgar su vida por rescatar a otros, a compartir lo poco de un país en emergencia humanitaria estancada. Aun teniendo poco, hemos dado con el corazón abierto. Esa solidaridad expresa lo mejor del país y demuestra que Venezuela cuenta con una reserva moral inmensa para enfrentar esta tragedia. Hoy Venezuela es solidaridad, dignidad y humanidad. Frente a las tragedias, nunca nos hemos resignarnos ni acostumbrarnos al dolor. While Russia lost two to three soldiers for every Ukrainian casualty for much of the war, this year it has suffered eight casualties for every one it inflicted on Ukraine. CSIS attributes the shift to Ukraine's intensified use of advanced drones, including some with AI-enabled targeting. IRAN •Qatar reported "positive progress" in indirect talks it mediated between the U.S. and Iran, but it sounds like all they really agreed on was to keep talking about the issues they still disagree on, like nuclear restrictions on Iran. •Talks are now on hold until after Iran concludes funeral ceremonies for former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in a U.S. airstrike on February 28. •Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf - Iran's parliament speaker and lead negotiator - called for a large turnout for Khamenei's funeral spectacle "so the world knows that the noble and honorable nation of Iran will not stay silent in the face of oppression and arrogance." He also called on the U.S. and Israel to "to avoid any miscalculations" during the processions. LIBYA •U.S. State Department officials hosted visitors from two of Libya's rival governments last week: Lt. Gen. Trump's Special Advisor, Massad Boulos, and AFRICOM Deputy Commander Lt. Gen. Brennan). •The Atlantic Council pointed out the optics of giving the leader of an armed faction an audience with the Secretary of State but snubbing the long over stayed UN anointed representative of an "interim government." •Moreover, The Atlantic Council suggests that entertaining the LNA's claims to power "formaliz[es] the families and patronage networks that already dominate" Libyan politics and "turns managed instability into a formal settlement." TRADE •Yesterday was the deadline to renew the U.S.-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) trilateral trade agreement, and - as anticipated - the U.S. opted not to lock in another 16-year term. Instead, the three neighbors will review the deal annually, giving them an opportunity to renegotiate key parts of the pact. •Pres. Trump has turned particularly critical of the deal, which he signed during his first term and once called "the fairest, most balanced, and beneficial trade agreement we have ever signed into law." He has since taken a tougher stance on trade and now hopes to squeeze more concessions from Canada and Mexico to close the U.S. trade deficit with its neighbors.

2026 war trends. First, the war business — the rise of Palantir-supported military capitalists who can never shut up about how much they love to kill, or at least watch others kill. With the most delightful technology, of course. Just how effective actually are these new heroes? I’ll also let you in on some recent claims by ‘Ukraine’s number 1 witch’ about strapons, witches, and scatplay. It’s relevant. And in parallel, a seemingly contradictory trend — the rise of Ukraine’s assault units. Instead of unmanned warfare, quite manned battle. With human ‘one-time uses’. It seems that despite all the bravado about a war of drones, it is human material that is becoming more necessary — and devalued — than ever. Third, losses. This year, a number of Ukrainian and pro-western sources have indicated Ukraine’s military losses to be increasing. AMK Mapping 🇳🇿 (@AMK_Mapping_) Preliminary figures for last night's combined missile and drone attack on Ukraine: ~30 Kh-101 cruise missiles launched, ~10 intercepted. ~24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles launched, ~6 intercepted. ~12 Zircon hypersonic cruise missiles launched, 0 intercepted. ~6 Kalibr cruise missiles launched, 6 intercepted. ~2 Kh-59/69 cruise missiles launched, 2 intercepted. ~74 missiles total, ~24 intercepted (~6/24 ballistics, ~18/50 cruise missiles). Air defence performed far more poorly this attack compared to the previous ones, despite still having quite a few Patriot interceptors. It seems that a large portion of the Patriot PAC-3 interceptors were wasted on trying to intercept Zircons, which are much harder to shoot down than Iskander-Ms. F-16s, Mirage-2000s, and IRIS-T interceptors worked quite well on the Kalibrs. They also did decently well east of Kyiv considering the fact that so many missiles were flying in at once, which overwhelmed air defence. However, the overall interception rate was far lower this time. These above figures are not final and will be further refined in the coming hours. Ukraine is working toward a just peace. Meanwhile, Russia, having failed to achieve its goals on the battlefield, is intensifying strikes on Ukrainian cities. Overnight, the enemy carried out one of the largest attacks on Ukraine: nearly 500 strike drones and 77 missiles, including 25 ballistic or hypersonic missiles. Thanks to the professionalism of our warriors and the support of our partners, more than 90% of cruise missiles and 90% of Shahed-type strike drones were intercepted. We thank our air defense forces, who protect Ukrainian skies every day and every night. At the same time, intercepting ballistic missiles remains a key challenge due to a shortage of missiles for Patriot systems. To secure the country with anti-ballistic missiles, in April the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine signed its first record contract for hundreds of PAC-2 missiles for Patriot, with Germany's support. Deliveries will begin over the coming years. For the first time, a step has also been taken toward purchasing around one hundred Patriot missiles worth $1 billion, financed through an EU loan. This year, Ukraine also began receiving missiles from European partners' stockpiles for the first time. In addition, through the implementation of the NATO After Action Review standard, Patriot effectiveness against maneuvering Iskander missiles has already more than doubled. But this is not enough — Ukraine critically needs additional missiles for its Patriot systems. They are available in partners' stockpiles. The protection of Ukrainian skies depends on fast decisions, the scaling of the PURL mechanism, and missile procurement through JUMPSTART. Ukraine's Minister of Defence has already sent letters to nearly 40 partner nations requesting the urgent transfer of Patriot missiles from existing stocks to Ukraine this month — in exchange for future deliveries already contracted for Ukraine. The Minister has also called on partners to contribute to the PURL and JUMPSTART mechanisms. These are the fastest and most reliable ways to supply the Patriot missiles Ukraine needs. It is critically important that decisions be made now, ahead of the NATO summit. The speed of our partners' decisions directly determines the protection of Ukrainian skies, critical infrastructure, and the lives of our people.

Türkiye’s Health Minister Prof Dr Kemal Memişoğlu and I signed the Istanbul Outcome Statement following the Ministerial Conference on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management. The statement calls on countries and partners to turn lessons into readiness people can count on: knowing the risks before earthquakes strike; preparing hospitals and clinics to keep essential services running; training and supporting emergency teams; and strengthening cooperation across sectors and borders so that care reaches people quickly and fairly. That call felt especially real as we heard from Mr Murat Genc, a volunteer from Türkiye’s National Medical Rescue Team (UMKE), who joined us online from Venezuela. His words showed what preparedness and solidarity mean in practice: trained teams reaching people when lives depend on fast, coordinated action. After the signing, Minister Memişoğlu and I joined UMKE volunteers for a photo, a powerful reminder that this agenda is ultimately about people ready to serve when others need them most. Microsoft is just one beneficiary of 250 years of American history and the choices made by past generations. As an American company, we believe we have a responsibility to understand where we have been, learn from it, and help make real for others the opportunities created for us. As America enters its 251st year, we face another inflection point shaped by rapid technological change. That is why we created this series. Throughout July, we will reflect on moments in American history with six video episodes when people faced uncertainty and made choices that set in motion consequences they could not fully see. Some decisions advanced the country. Others revealed how much work remained. Together, they remind us that history is not inevitable; it is made by people, in moments, through choices. Our goal is not simply to celebrate that history, but to learn and connect the past to the questions we face today. John Adams, writing to Abigail, about the Continental Congress' vote in favor of independence on July 2, 1776: "The Second Day of July 1776, will be the most memorable Epocha, in the History of America. I am apt to believe that it will be celebrated, by succeeding Generations, as the great anniversary Festival. It ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations from one End of this Continent to the other from this Time forward forever more. You will think me transported with Enthusiasm but I am not. -- I am well aware of the Toil and Blood and Treasure, that it will cost Us to maintain this Declaration, and support and defend these States. -- Yet through all the Gloom I can see the Rays of ravishing Light and Glory. I can see that the End is more than worth all the Means. And that Posterity will tryumph in that Days Transaction, even altho We should rue it, which I trust in God We shall not."

If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, and Prof. K. V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, participated in a panel discussion on "Data, Statistics and India's Growth Agenda", held as part of "Swarna Andhra @ 2047: Economic Intelligence for Governance", a two-day capacity-building programme organised by the Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh. The panel was moderated by Shri Suresh Goyal, Director General, NCAER, and featured Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India; and Prof. S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman, EAC-PM, as fellow panellists. Dr. Balasubramaniam emphasised that data must serve as a foundation for dignity in governance, making visible those often overlooked in averages, including informal workers and tribal communities. He noted that while India already has rich individual-level data, the priority now is to harmonise datasets across ministries, break institutional silos, and use evidence to strengthen social development and citizen capability. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat, he stressed that better decisions depend on engaging with what the data truly reveals and viewing citizens as active participants in the development journey. The programme's broader context was set by Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu, whose address emphasised translating the State's growth vision into measurable, mission-mode outcomes, integrating datasets across departments and geographies, and pursuing growth that is sustainable and inclusive. @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp @drrbalu

Based on visible automatic identification system (AIS) data from MarineTraffic.com, roughly two-thirds of transiting vessels continued to use the Iranian (northern) traffic separation scheme, while the remaining traffic utilized the Omani (southern) route. Syrian State TV has confirmed that the explosion at a café earlier today, which killed and wounded several people, was caused by an explosive device. The incident comes as Syria continues to face a fragile security environment despite a reduction in large-scale fighting. While many areas of the country have seen improved stability, attacks involving improvised explosive devices (IEDs), targeted assassinations, and operations by extremist cells, including remnants of ISIS, continue to pose a persistent threat, particularly in urban centers and contested regions. Authorities have not yet identified those responsible for today's bombing, and the investigation remains ongoing. Video

In a major international effort to evaluate potential treatments for #Ebola disease due to Bundibugyo virus (BVD), the PARTNERS (Platform Adaptive Randomised Trial for New and Repurposed Filovirus TreatmentS) clinical trial has opened enrolment today for patients in the #DRC. What does the trial do? This trial will assess whether two therapies – ➡️ a monoclonal antibody (MBP134) ➡️ an antiviral medicine (remdesivir) can improve survival among people diagnosed with BVD. It will also evaluate whether combining the two provides additional benefits. Who is behind it? The trial, sponsored by the WHO, has been coordinated by the Institut National pour la Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in the DRC, the @ITMantwerp Institute of Tropical Medicine in Belgium, and the @UniofOxford in the United Kingdom, in collaboration with international research, clinical and humanitarian partners, and supported by @AfricaCDC. What can the trials help determine? The PARTNERS trial is expected to assess whether these therapies can improve outcomes for patients with BVD and reduce deaths in affected communities. 🔗 bit.ly/4fgBtn2

"Yesterday, President @EmmanuelMacron of #France and I published a joint op-ed about the impact of #SocialMedia and other digital environments on the health of young people. In the past year, several governments including Australia, Canada, France, Indonesia, Ireland, Spain and the United Kingdom have all introduced measures to protect children from online harm. Together, these measures reflect a growing global consensus that digital environments require effective governance, accountability, age-appropriate design, and stronger safeguards to protect child health. Digital environments are not neutral. How they are designed, governed, and monetized shapes many aspects of our lives, including health. For example, repeated exposure to stereotyped, sexualized, violent, or discriminatory content shapes how children understand themselves and the world around them. It can also lead children to make unrealistic comparisons with others, undermining their confidence and self-esteem. Algorithms increasingly filter health information to increase attention and engagement rather than accuracy, allowing misleading claims to spread. And features including infinite scrolling, auto-play, personalized content and push notifications increase the risk for addictive behaviour. The collection and use of personal data, particularly for profiling and targeted marketing, raise concerns about privacy, manipulation, and well-being. WHO is responding to these concerns by strengthening research, advising countries, and promoting safe, equitable digital health environments. Preventing exposure to illegal or extreme and graphic content is essential. But children’s well-being requires more than the absence of harm. It depends on stable relationships, appropriate boundaries, physical activity, and opportunities for real-world social connection. Above all, we must listen to young people. They are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity. They are our future. Together, we can – and must – shape digital environments that protect and support their health"-@DrTedros nitter.perennialte.ch/DrTedros/status/207226… Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (@DrTedros) Digital spaces bring opportunities, but also risks for children’s health and development. Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, on 2 July 2026, met over dinner with H.E. Dato’ Sri Tiong King Sing, Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture of Malaysia, on the sidelines of the 39th Asia-Pacific Roundtable, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment to strengthening ASEAN tourism and cultural cooperation, advancing the implementation of the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, the ASEAN Economic Community Strategic Plan 2026–2030, and the ASEAN Tourism Sectoral Plan 2026–2030. The discussions focused on enhancing regional connectivity, promoting sustainable and quality tourism, safeguarding cultural heritage, while developing a thriving cultural and creative industries ecosystem, strengthening engagement with Dialogue Partners of ASEAN, and fostering a more resilient, inclusive, and competitive ASEAN tourism and vibrant culture and arts sectors.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today delivered a closing address at the 39th Asia-Pacific Roundtable, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, highlighting the “Power of ASEAN Conviction” in navigating an increasingly complex regional and global landscape. Dr. Kao underscored ASEAN’s enduring commitment to advancing peace, prosperity, a sustainable planet, people-centred development, meaningful partnerships, as well as future potentials and possibilities. Dr. Kao reaffirmed the importance of ASEAN centrality, unity, inclusivity, and collective action in shaping a stable, resilient and prosperous region. He also commended the ASEAN-Institutes of Strategic and International Studies (ASEAN-ISIS) network for its longstanding contribution to strategic dialogue and regional cooperation. Türkiye’s Health Minister Prof Dr Kemal Memişoğlu and I signed the Istanbul Outcome Statement following the Ministerial Conference on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management. The statement calls on countries and partners to turn lessons into readiness people can count on: knowing the risks before earthquakes strike; preparing hospitals and clinics to keep essential services running; training and supporting emergency teams; and strengthening cooperation across sectors and borders so that care reaches people quickly and fairly. That call felt especially real as we heard from Mr Murat Genc, a volunteer from Türkiye’s National Medical Rescue Team (UMKE), who joined us online from Venezuela. His words showed what preparedness and solidarity mean in practice: trained teams reaching people when lives depend on fast, coordinated action. After the signing, Minister Memişoğlu and I joined UMKE volunteers for a photo, a powerful reminder that this agenda is ultimately about people ready to serve when others need them most. Teşekkürler Türkiye and Minister Memişoğlu for hosting this important conference and for your leadership in advancing this agenda. La mayoría de esos pueblos votaron por Abelardo. Esos 95 pueblos en su mayoría en Boyacá, Antioquia, Santander, Cundinamarca y Tolima le dieron 92.000 de diferencia a favor de Abelardo, que en Colombia ganó por 72.000 votos. Todos estos pueblos con poblaciones muy por debajo del promedio Colombiano pero con un censo electoral singularmente comparable con el de su población prefirieron a Abelardo. 150 pueblos con un censo electoral mayor al 95% de la población estimada de los mismos le dieron una ventaja de 274,197 votos a Abelardo. (suficientes para ganar las elecciones). 250 pueblos (estos incluyen los antes mencionados) con más del 90% de la población registrada como votantes le dieron a Abelardo una ventaja de 384,215 votos. 397 pueblos (también incluyendo los anteriores) con más del 85% de su población registrada como votantes le dieron a Abelardo una ventaja de 564,914. This demonstration shows how @elonmusk's Starlink could help keep communities connected when traditional networks are unavailable.

Shri Dipak Barman, Minister for School Education, Government of West Bengal, and Shri Jagannath Chattopadhyay, Minister for Higher Education, Government of West Bengal, called on Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, for discussions on key priorities concerning the education sector in the State. The discussions focused on strengthening school and higher education in West Bengal, with emphasis on improving educational infrastructure, expanding girls’ hostel facilities, ensuring access to STEM education across all schools, enhancing the implementation of PM eVIDYA and the e-SMARTH portal, and strengthening the effective functioning of existing systems and institutional mechanisms. Deliberations also covered the establishment of AVGC Content Creator Labs, the development of university townships, and measures to facilitate the entry of foreign universities while positioning West Bengal’s universities as preferred destinations for international students. The proposed initiatives are expected to benefit all districts of the State by expanding access to quality education and fostering large-scale educational development aligned with international standards. करण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी दिले. आदिवासी विकास विभागासाठी राबविण्यात येणाऱ्या विविध शैक्षणिक व कल्याणकारी योजनांमधील उत्पन्न मर्यादेचा पुनर्विचार करून अधिकाधिक आदिवासी विद्यार्थ्यांना योजनांचा लाभ मिळेल यासाठी किमान ₹4,00,000 उत्पन्न मर्यादा करण्याबाबतची कार्यवाही करावी. अनुसूचित जमाती प्रमाणपत्र तपासणी अधिनियमामधील सुधारणा प्रक्रियेला गती देणे, प्रकल्प अधिकारी, रिक्त पदे, न्यायालयीन प्रकरणांसाठी विशेष विधिज्ञांची नियुक्ती आणि प्रशासकीय कार्यक्षमता वाढविण्याबाबत संबंधित विभागांनी समन्वयाने कार्यवाही करावी. आदिवासी विकास विभागामार्फत इतर विभागांना वितरित होणाऱ्या निधीचे प्रभावी नियंत्रण व योजनांचे नियमित मूल्यमापन करण्यासाठी राज्यस्तरीय व जिल्हास्तरीय यंत्रणा अधिक सक्षम करण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. वनहक्क कायद्याच्या प्रभावी H.E. San Lwin, Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for the ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community, led ASEAN Secretariat delegations for a site visit to the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre), as part of the 2nd Regional Forum on the ASCC Strategic Plan, on 1 July 2026. The site visit was also attended by Mr. Chujo Kazuo, Chargé d'affaires ad interim and Minister/Deputy Head of the Mission of Japan to ASEAN, and delegations from ASEAN Member States, ASEAN Centres and Entities, Civil Service Organisations (CSOs), Research Organisations/Think Thanks, ASEAN Dialogue Partners, and the ASEAN Secretariat. In his key message, H.E. San Lwin highlighted the AHA Centre’s role in regional disaster management, humanitarian assistance, and disaster risk reduction. He shared that the AHA Centre serves as an example where regional commitments meet concrete action and tangible results. In his welcome remark, Mr. Krishna Putra Tanaja, Deputy Executive Director of the AHA Centre, welcomed all delegations and participants and highlighted how the ASCC Strategic Plan laid a foundation for more resilient region in facing future emergencies. Site visit participants listened to the presentation on the work of the AHA Centre, particularly on the Centre’s day-to-day monitoring, and process in mobilisation, coordination and assistance in time of disaster responses. Participants exchanged views on ways to strengthen regional, national, and local resilience to emerging climate-induced disasters, and strategies to institutionalise regional commitments into national plans and policies. The 2nd Regional Forum on the ASCC Strategic Plan is part of the “Supporting the Development of the ASCC 1 July 2026 Strategic Plan” project supported by the Government of Japan through the Japan-ASEAN Integration Fund (JAIF) 3.0. #ASEAN #ASEANCommunity #ASCCStrategicPlan #ASCCPost2025 #JapanASEANIntegrationFund #JAIF #ACV2045

Mission deployed #INSTrikand, a stealth frigate of the #IndianNavy operating in the Gulf of Aden, responded swiftly to the reported piracy attempt and arrived in the vicinity of the vessel early on #02Jul 26. The Master of MV Golden Arsenal confirmed the safety of all crew members despite damage to the bridge superstructure and adjoining compartments. Specialist teams from #INSTrikand boarded the vessel and carried out sanitisation operation. No suspicious personnel were found onboard. Subsequently, the Indian Navy team safely moved the crew from the citadel and assisted in restoring the vessel to operational readiness for the continuation of her voyage. #IndianNavy P8I also undertook aerial surveillance and reconnaissance in support of the operation. With anti-piracy operations concluded and the vessel rendered safe for further transit, MV Golden Arsenal has resumed her voyage. The response to the aftermath of Russia’s attack is still ongoing in Kyiv: first responders are clearing the rubble, searching for people, and providing assistance. Damage has been reported at more than 20 sites across the city, most of them ordinary residential buildings. There was also damage to an ambulance station, a research institute, a hotel, and businesses. As of now, we know that, tragically, 13 people were killed in this Russian strike. My condolences to their families and loved ones. More than 90 others were injured. Everyone who needs help is receiving all necessary assistance. Five people were wounded in the Kharkiv region, including a child, and two more in the Kyiv region, where civilian infrastructure was also targeted. Overnight, Russia also struck the Sumy, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, and Cherkasy regions. In total, Russia launched more than 70 missiles of various types against Ukraine overnight, nearly half of them ballistic missiles, along with almost 500 attack drones, including jet-powered “shaheds.” The main strike was directed at Kyiv. Our air defenders managed to shoot down a significant number of the incoming targets, but not all of them. Air defense supplies for Ukraine are an absolute and critical priority. Contributions to the PURL program remain essential – they directly help save lives. Every bilateral agreement we reach with our partners on air defense truly makes a difference. I am grateful to every leader who is helping. It is especially important that we move forward with implementing our agreements on the production of anti-ballistic capabilities. We also very much count on a decision by the United States regarding licenses for Patriots and other forms of cooperation. These are the kinds of steps that can stop this war and prevent attacks like this. I thank everyone who stands with Ukraine, with our people, and with our efforts to protect life. Video

Starting in early 2025, Elon Musk and the Trump administration began terminating USAID's programs and firing its staff — with Musk himself boasting about "feeding it into the woodchipper." One year ago today, USAID was officially dissolved, its remaining programs haphazardly folded into the State Department. Amid all the lies and misinformation that have followed, some facts about what has actually been lost: • USAID saved more than 3 million lives a year at a cost of less than $10/month per American. That is what was destroyed. On purpose. • According to Boston University's Global Impact Counter — which tracked deaths attributable to the cuts until it stopped operations in February 2026 — an estimated 781,000 people died preventable deaths in the first year, including 518,000 children. • Global child mortality (the number of children who die before their fifth birthday) rose in 2025 for the first time in 35+ years — by 200,000 additional deaths. • USAID's 50-country disease surveillance network — the system that cut outbreak response times from 2 weeks to 48 hours — is gone. We are now watching an unprecedented Ebola outbreak unfold in real time — with the highest first-month caseload and death rate in modern history. • Programs reaching 93 million women and children were cut 92%. TB programs cut 56%. Water and sanitation cut 86%. Over 2,000 health facilities permanently closed. • 25 million fewer people received humanitarian assistance in 2025. The overall humanitarian budget was slashed 74% — from $14.1 billion to $3.7 billion. • 363 million people face acute hunger in 2026. The famine early-warning system that would have seen it coming went dark for five months. • $1.7 billion in democracy and governance funding (election monitoring, anti-corruption work, support for independent media and civil society) was terminated. • 360+ independent media outlets lost funding. Hundreds of legal clinics closed. • Far from saving money, the Trump administration itself has already said the dismantlement will cost taxpayers at least $19.2 billion in cancellation fees, severance, and penalties. That's more than half of USAID's annual budget — spent on destruction and closeout, not support for vulnerable people. • American farmers, universities, and businesses are among the casualties too. USAID partnered with more than 3,500 U.S. companies and maintained 17 university-based research labs. Its work with U.S.-based contractors and the private sector generated hundreds of thousands of American jobs and multiplied the return on every dollar spent. Those markets and partnerships are gone.

Personal de la División Narcotráfico Metropolitana de ARCA-DGA y de la División Operaciones Federales de la PFA llevó adelante tareas conjuntas, entre ellas el análisis del teléfono celular secuestrado, el seguimiento digital de la compra de pasajes aéreos y el entrecruzamiento de datos bancarios y financieros. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, inaugurated the Global Institute for Future Technologies (GIFT) at JSS Academy of Higher Education & Research, Mysuru. Addressing the gathering, he reflected on how technological change is reshaping the world of work and underscored the need to view skills as part of a broader ecosystem of knowledge, entrepreneurship and innovation. As industries evolve, he noted, institutions must also reimagine how capabilities are developed and assessed so that learners are equipped to respond to emerging opportunities and create new ones. Emphasising that India's journey towards Viksit Bharat will be anchored in a knowledge-driven economy, Dr. Balasubramaniam highlighted the importance of institutions that bring together interdisciplinary learning, research, innovation and enterprise. Such ecosystems play a critical role in strengthening human capital, fostering innovation and translating knowledge into solutions for national development. It is equally a problem of governance, institutional coordination, and existential threats that larger powers rarely confront. A new book review by Ms Kripa Anand of the National Maritime Foundation examines Blue Security in the Indo-Pacific, edited by Ian Hall, Troy Lee-Brown, and Rebecca Strating — a volume spanning eighteen country case studies, from Australia's declining naval capability to Papua New Guinea's 3.12 million square kilometre EEZ governed by a state whose nearest police base to some of its most remote maritime territories is hundreds of kilometres away. The findings are uncomfortable — and consequential. En plena pandemia, fue uno de los pocos que salió de su casa a trabajar con su moto de delivery, mientras la mayoría estaba encerrada por el coronavirus. Pero no volvió. Esa noche fue embestido por una camioneta que circulaba por la avenida Corrientes. El conductor, Sebastián Gabriel Di Pietro, circulaba con exceso de velocidad, bajo los efectos de la cocaína y la marihuana. Tenía, además, 1,9 gramos de alcohol en sangre. Después de casi seis años del choque que se cobró la vida del repartidor, este martes, Di Pietro comenzó a cumplir la condena a cuatro años y seis meses de prisión por el homicidio vial. Según pudo saber Infobae, el hombre se presentó junto a su defensor en el Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal y Correccional N°19, luego de que la Corte Suprema de Justicia rechazara el último recurso presentado por su defensa y dejara firme la sentencia. Di Pietro quedó detenido en la sede judicial y fue alojado de manera provisoria en la Comisaría Vecinal 1B de la Policía de la Ciudad, donde permanecerá hasta que se le asigne un cupo en una unidad del Servicio Penitenciario Federal. 𝟐𝐧𝐝 𝐉𝐮𝐥𝐲, 𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟐 | 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐬’ 𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐨𝐟 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐁𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐭 𝐒𝐢𝐦𝐥𝐚 On this day in 1972, India entered the Simla Agreement after its decisive victory in the 1971 war. With over 𝟗𝟑,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐏𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐢 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐰𝐚𝐫 and captured territory, India was negotiating from an unprecedented position of strength. Yet, instead of converting that leverage into a lasting settlement of key issues, especially Kashmir, the Congress leadership chose a framework centred on just bilateral dialogue. The poor diplomatic policy put in place by Congress during the Simla Agreement remains one of independent India's biggest missed strategic opportunities. A moment of overwhelming advantage became the subject of decades of debate over whether India gave away too much without securing a permanent resolution. Over five decades later, 𝟐𝐧𝐝 𝐉𝐮𝐥𝐲 and 𝐒𝐢𝐦𝐥𝐚 𝐀𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 continue to raise important questions about diplomacy, negotiation and the Congress’ intent towards resolution of the Pakistan problem.

Why doesn’t India buy Turkish drones? Because India doesn’t need them. Three reasons: 1️⃣ Strategic trust: Turkey openly prioritizes Pakistan for its drone exports and defence cooperation. Depending on a supplier closely aligned with your adversary is a strategic risk. 2️⃣ Better capability: India has already moved to the MQ-9B Predator class—far beyond the Bayraktar TB2 in endurance, payload, SATCOM connectivity, and maritime surveillance. 3️⃣ Make in India: India is investing billions in indigenous drones, swarming systems, loitering munitions, TAPAS, Ghatak, CATS Warrior, and domestic manufacturing partnerships. The future of India’s drone power won’t be imported from Ankara—it will be built in India and strengthened with trusted strategic partners. 🇮🇳🛡️

En el último avance que publiqué sobre el rescate de Hernán, llevábamos 28 horas de trabajo. Ahora ya son 58 horas y aún no hemos logrado sacarlo. La dificultad es que Hernán se encuentra atrapado dentro de una estructura de nueve pisos sumamente inestable, y el túnel que habíamos excavado ha sufrido varios derrumbes. Equipos de rescate de varios países han estado trabajando juntos sin descanso para estabilizar el túnel, apuntalándolo, reforzándolo y aislándolo, pero no ha sido posible sostenerlo. Por lo que se ha tomado la decisión de abrir, de forma paralela, un nuevo túnel desde otro punto, donde podría haber una mayor posibilidad de avanzar con seguridad. Sin embargo, toda la estructura sigue corriendo el riesgo de colapsar, y no descartamos retomar el túnel original en el que nuestros equipos han trabajado durante estas 58 horas, si las condiciones lo permiten. A pesar de todo, no hemos perdido la comunicación con Hernán y continuamos suministrándole líquidos para mantenerlo hidratado. Hernán sigue luchando, y nosotros también. Primero Dios, lograremos rescatarlo. Video Nayib Bukele (@nayibbukele) Llevamos 28 horas tratando de rescatar de los escombros a Hernán Alberto Gil Flores, de 44 años, quien permanece atrapado en el centro comercial Galerías Playa Grande. Equipos de varios países nos están ayudando a lograrlo, ya que la complejidad de la estructura, su inestabilidad, las lluvias de ayer y las réplicas han hecho de este uno de los rescates más difíciles que hemos enfrentado. Sin embargo, a pesar de todas estas dificultades, Hernán continúa respondiendo y hemos logrado mantenerlo hidratado, por lo que tenemos la esperanza de que este rescate será un éxito. Con la ayuda de Dios, lo lograremos. Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/nayibbukele/status/2072003346873880907#m

The U.S./Iran War isn’t over… it’s just far more covert. Right now, we are seeing an increasingly dangerous battle take place in the Strait of Hormuz. Under what some are calling Operation Freedom 2.0, the United States is escorting (via air cover) vessels through the Omani side of the Strait. More and more, this is being conducted via convoys of 3-5 vessels at a time, and in both directions. Here is why this is… complicated and risky. Since the dueling blockades between Iran and the United States was unofficially lifted on June 15th, it has quickly become a battle of who can leverage this window more effectively to their advantage. Thus far, there is little argument that Iran has seen more benefit, with recent data showing they exported 50M barrels in the first 14 days alone. A rate double of their normal daily exports. However, in THEORY, the United States can create a de facto unwinding of global economic damage by providing sufficient air support to maximize the exports of global oil in a manner and rate that is disproportionately favorable to the United States. Given that pipelines are moving some 7M barrels per day, and normal oil flows through the Strait is 20M/day, that means they need to force through at MINIMUM 13Mbpd to stagnate the losses… but not unwind them. In order to unwind, they would be needing to export beyond normal flows. The challenge here though… the math is just very hard to justify this. Iran still has a SIGNIFICANT amount of oil in onshore storage (~60M), plus oil already loaded onto vessels in the Strait (~10M). Given that Iran isexporting at approximately double the standard rate (3.4Mbpd since blockade lifting vs 1.7Mbpd pre-conflict exports), and can maintain this rate for several more weeks with the ~70M barrels already produced, they can rapidly unwind the damages of the blockade through these exports. The United States and the global economy on the other hand... They're barely able to even reach normal export rates via the Omani route, much less exceed it to such a degree that they can begin unwinding the 1.1B of barrels unproduced during this conflict. And what are the risks here? Already, we have seen at least one Apache Helicopter get shot down by Iran. Several vessels transiting via this route have been struck by Iran. And the two Apache aviators? Nobody has yet heard a word from them. What happens if Americans are killed providing air coverage for this route? What happens if an American is shot down and captured? Will Trump be forced to return back to all out war? The risk/reward calculus simply doesn't make sense. The math doesn't work. The strategy isn't viable. Washington needs to quickly come to their sense before Iran re-closes the Strait, or before Americans are needlessly killed.

NIH scientists found that retinal organoids, lab-grown models of the human retina, often don't get enough oxygen during early development. The Indus River Basin sustains one of the world’s largest contiguous irrigation systems, provides over 80 percent of Pakistan’s agricultural water needs, and supports the lives and livelihoods of over 240 million people. For more than six decades, the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) of 1960 has provided a time-tested framework for equitable and predictable management of the waters of the Indus River basin. India’s unilateral decision to hold the Treaty in abeyance last year in April, followed by material breaches; including unannounced disruptions of downstream flows and withholding of hydrological information; has created an unprecedented crisis for Pakistan’s water security and for regional stability. This is not nature's doing. This is a nation state deliberately weaponizing water. Pakistan’s position is unequivocal; the Treaty remains legally intact and permits no unilateral suspension or modification. Ishaq Dar (@MIshaqDar50) It was a privilege to address the seminar, “Indus Waters Treaty: An Instrument of Regional Peace and Stability,” where leading experts from Pakistan and abroad discussed one of the defining challenges of our time in South Asia. I underscored that the Indus Waters Treaty is not merely a water-sharing arrangement but a vital instrument of regional peace, stability, and cooperation. Shared waters must never be weaponized. They must remain a bridge between nations, guided by cooperation, dialogue, and respect for international law. Any attempt to deprive Pakistan of its rights under the Treaty would have profound consequences for regional peace and security, undermining the shared interests of nearly two billion people of South Asia. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/MIshaqDar50/status/2071935862238232887#m

With Russia offering Su-57 cooperation and China expanding its regional influence, the US knows this window won’t remain open forever. The deal remains unnamed. But the direction of travel is becoming increasingly clear.

"Our friends went to the court, and we went to the court. The Court of Arbitration, from our point of view, gave a mixed judgment. Sometimes it ruled in our favour, and sometimes it ruled in favour of our neighbouring country. Everyone accepted that we would go with whatever the international court decided. The court passed a judgment and placed limits on the technical design of the flow of water. It set clear limits and decided how it was going to be managed. No country can unilaterally decide what the design is going to be. No country can decide how it is going to stop the flow of water from one country to another. And guess what? One country stood up and said, "I do not accept that jurisdiction. I do not accept the court's jurisdiction." So, what then is the jurisdiction of international courts of justice? None? Does that mean tomorrow any country, including any nuclear state, can simply stand up and say, "I don't accept your jurisdiction. I don't accept the world order. I don't accept treaties. I don't accept rights. I don't accept justice. I simply don't accept"? So, ladies and gentlemen, to me, the treaty has been revealed, and with it, all the treaties of the world have been revealed. This is not just a message for us. We can take care of ourselves, as we have seen. No one can stop our water. But what about the rest of the world? If this precedent has been set, and if the new world order is to be shaped according to this new precedent, then what about the rest of the world?" #IndusWatersTreaty Video

He has never missed a meal in his life – but he is the most envious of the Man – the producer, the entrepreneur… 2. “Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy” – the ideology is manufactured from the start, designed not to free the animals but to direct their resentment away from the pigs and toward a useful target. Every revolution needs an enemy. The pigs chose the farmer. 3. The revolution’s commandments were never a constitution. They were a management tool – sacred enough to motivate, vague enough to rewrite, and controlled from the beginning by the only ones who could read – the pigs. 4. Boxer the horse, the most honest creature on the farm, decent, loyal yet naive, totally devoted, responds to every setback with the same answer: “I will work harder!” He means it completely. He works himself half to death. It is the most heartbreaking sentence in the book – because the new system is perfectly designed to absorb exactly that kind of devotion and give nothing back. When he finally collapses from exhaustion, he is sold to the knacker. For cash. The pigs buy more whisky with the proceeds. The other animals are told he died in a hospital receiving the best care. The most useful animal on the farm is the one who never once suspects he is the product. 5. The commandments get rewritten at night not because power corrupted the revolution – the rewriting was always the plan. Language was the weapon from the first speech Old Major ever gave. 6. “All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others” – this is not the system’s failure. It is the system’s true face, finally visible once the animals are too exhausted and confused to object. 7. Orwell’s message: the lie came first. And the "liberation" it promised delivered something far worse than what came before – because the fattest pig was merely selfish at the start, but by the end is selfish and fluent in the language of "justice." He took all the eggs. He took everything. And made the hens thank him for it. UNRWA, a lifeline for millions of Palestine refugees, is far more than a humanitarian agency. It embodies the international community's collective responsibility toward the Palestinian people and enjoys privileges and immunities under international law. The reported funding shortfall of $220 million threatens to disrupt the delivery of essential services to millions of Palestine refugees who depend on the Agency's support. We believe that UNRWA's mandate must be preserved, strengthened, and adequately funded. We also call for accountability for the killing of 392 UNRWA personnel since the outbreak of the conflict in Gaza. UNRWA cannot be divorced from the core final-status issue of Palestine refugees. The solution is not to dismantle the Agency, but to end the Israeli occupation, enable the return of Palestine refugees in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, and realize the two-State solution based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as the capital of an independent, sovereign State of Palestine.

आधुनिक शेती आणि शेतकरी सक्षमीकरणासाठी राज्य सरकार कटिबद्ध सन 2023 व 2024 या वर्षात कृषी क्षेत्रात उल्लेखनीय कार्य करणाऱ्या शेतकरी व अधिकाऱ्यांच्या सन्मानार्थ मुंबई येथे आयोजित 'कृषी सन्मान व पुरस्कार वितरण समारंभ 2026' कार्यक्रमास राज्यपाल जिष्णू देव वर्मा आणि मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी प्रमुख उपस्थिती दर्शविली. कृषी क्षेत्रात उल्लेखनीय कार्य केलेल्या सर्व पुरस्कारार्थींचा हा सन्मान केवळ औपचारिक सन्मान नसून आपल्या कृषी संस्कृतीचा गौरव आहे. प्रतिकूल परिस्थितीतही प्रयोगशील आणि नावीन्यपूर्ण शेती करून इतर शेतकऱ्यांसाठी प्रेरणादायी ठरलेले पुरस्कार विजेते शेतकरी हेच कृषी विभागाचे खरे राजदूत असल्याचे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी केले. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले, राज्यातील शेती अधिक सक्षम, शाश्वत आणि फायदेशीर करण्यासाठी जलसंधारण, सौर कृषी पंप, दिवसा मोफत वीज, कृषी यांत्रिकीकरण, प्रमाणित बियाणे, सिंचन सुविधा आणि शेतकऱ्यांना आर्थिक आधार अशा विविध योजनांद्वारे राज्य सरकार सातत्याने काम करत असून, महाराष्ट्राच्या पुढील पिढीला दुष्काळाची झळ बसू देणार नाही. राज्यात जलयुक्त शिवार अभियान आणि 'मागेल त्याला शेततळे' योजनेच्या माध्यमातून 22,000 हून अधिक गावांमध्ये जलसंधारणाची व्यापक कामे करण्यात आली आहेत. या कामांमुळे अनेक भागांमध्ये एक पिकावरून दोन आणि तीन पिकांची शेती शक्य झाली असून, ज्या भागात शेती करणे कठीण होते, त्या ठिकाणीही फळबागा फुलू लागल्या आहेत. हवामान बदलाच्या आव्हानांवर मात करण्यासाठी जलसंधारण हा प्रभावी उपाय ठरत आहे. राज्यातील शेतकऱ्यांना मोफत वीज देण्याचा निर्णय प्रभावीपणे राबविण्यात येत असून, सौर कृषी पंपांच्या स्थापनेत महाराष्ट्र देशात आघाडीवर आहे. या योजनेअंतर्गत देशभरात बसविण्यात आलेल्या सौर कृषी पंपांपैकी सुमारे 60% हून अधिक पंप महाराष्ट्रात बसविण्यात आले आहेत. सध्या 75% शेतकऱ्यांना दिवसा वीज उपलब्ध होत असून, चालू वर्षाअखेर राज्यातील सर्व शेतकऱ्यांना दिवसा 12 तास मोफत वीज उपलब्ध करून देण्याचे उद्दिष्ट असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, शेतकऱ्यांना मोफत वीज पुरविण्यासाठी राज्य सरकार दरवर्षी ₹28000 कोटी खर्च करत आहे. कृषी यांत्रिकीकरणासाठी दरवर्षी ₹1500 ते 2000 कोटींची तरतूद करण्यात बियाण्यांवर प्रभावी नियंत्रण मिळविणे शक्य होईल. राज्यातील दुष्काळी भागांना दीर्घकालीन दिलासा मिळावा यासाठी फ्लड डायव्हर्जनच्या माध्यमातून अतिरिक्त पाणी पश्चिम महाराष्ट्रातील दुष्काळी तालुक्यांपर्यंत 🇮🇳🇺🇸 Washington may finally have found the formula for India: partnership, not pressure. At the US-India Strategic Partnership Forum, Ambassador Sergio Gor hinted that another major US-India deal is close. More interesting than the deal itself was the message: Boeing featured directly in discussions between Donald Trump and Narendra Modi. The timing aligns with two major programmes already in motion: six additional P-8I maritime patrol aircraft and the GE F414 engine agreement with unprecedented technology transfer for production in India. Gor’s remark that “India’s rise is here, India has arrived” suggests Washington increasingly sees New Delhi not just as a defence customer, but as a strategic industrial partner. With Russia offering Su-57 cooperation and China expanding its regional influence, the US knows this window won’t remain open forever. The deal remains unnamed. But the direction of travel is becoming increasingly clear.

🚨 OSINT | Moscow Under Renewed Long-Range Strike Ukraine’s deep-strike campaign is no longer about headlines—it’s becoming a sustained effort to erode Russia’s military command network. Reports indicate a fresh strike on the Dubna satellite communications centre north of Moscow—the second reported attack on the facility in just over a week. Kyiv says the site supports Russian military command, intelligence and battlefield communications, while Moscow says it intercepted hundreds of incoming drones during the latest assault. OSINT Assessment: • Repeated strikes on the same target suggest Ukraine believes the facility remains operational or has been only partially degraded. • Russia is increasingly compelled to divert valuable air-defence assets toward protecting the capital and strategic infrastructure. • The campaign reflects a shift from isolated deep strikes to persistent pressure on Russia’s C4ISR backbone. The battle is no longer confined to the front line. It is steadily expanding into Russia’s strategic rear, where every successful strike forces difficult choices about what can—and cannot—be defended.

اسلام آباد: 1 جولائی 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیر صدارت ملک میں دانش سکولوں اور دانش یونیورسٹی کے قیام پر جائزہ اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ دانش سکول اور دانش یونیورسٹی انتہائی اہم قومی اثاثہ ہیں. ملک بھر میں دانش سکولوں اور اسلام آباد میں دانش یونیورسٹی کی تعمیر قوم کے تابناک مستقبل کے لیے بہترین سرمایہ کاری ہے. وزیرِ اعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ مظفر آباد میں دانش یونیورسٹی کا Tech کیمپس بنایا جائے اور چاروں صوبوں، گلگت بلتستان اور آزاد جموں و کشمیر میں دانش سکولوں کی تعمیر جلد از جلد مکمل کی جائے. وزیرِ اعظم نے دانش سکولوں کا ڈیزائن علاقائی ثقافت سے ہم آہنگ کرنے کی بھی ہدایت کی. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ دانش سکولوں اور یونیورسٹی میں تدریسی اور دیگر عملے کی بھرتی خالصتاً میرٹ پر کی جائے. وزیراعظم نے دانش سکولوں کی تعمیر کے حوالے سے تیز پیشرفت پر وفاقی وزارت تعلیم و پیشہ ورانہ تربیت کی ٹیم کی پزیرائی کی. اجلاس میں وزیراعظم کو خیبر پختونخوا، سندھ، بلوچستان، گلگت بلتستان، آزاد جموں و کشمیر اور اسلام آباد میں 27 دانش سکولوں اور اسلام آباد میں دانش یونیورسٹی کی تعمیر کی پیشرفت کے حوالے سے آگاہ کیا گیا. بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ دانش سکول کری اسلام آباد کی تعمیر مکمل ہو چکی ہے اور سکول میں تدریس کا آغاز ہو چکا ہے. باغ، بھمبر، سلطان آباد، گانشے اور استور میں دانش سکولوں کی تعمیر مکمل ہونے کو ہے اور اپریل 2027 سے کلاسز شروع ہو جائینگی. اجلاس کو مزید بتایا گیا کہ دانش یونیورسٹی میں تدریسی عملے کی بھرتی کے عمل کا آغاز کیا گیا ہے. دانش یونیورسٹی میں2027 سے کلاسز کا آغاز ہو گا اور ملک بھر بالخصوص پسماندہ علاقوں سے میرٹ کی بنیاد پر طلباء کو داخلہ دیا جائے گا. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزراء اعظم نذیر تارڑ، احسن اقبال، عطاء اللہ تارڑ، خالد مقبول صدیقی اور متعلقہ اداروں کے اعلیٰ افسران شریک تھے۔ Video

Deputy Prime Minister /Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a Committee meeting to review the existing Guidelines for the Establishment of Universities and Higher Education Institutions in Pakistan. The committee reviewed the draft 2026 HEC Regulatory Framework for the Establishment and Accreditation of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in Pakistan. The revlevant stakeholders provided a detailed briefing to the Committee about this policy. The committee appreciated the efforts of the Higher Education Commission (HEC), and recommended improvements in certain areas. DPM/ FM further directed HEC to incorporate recommendations provided by this committee and submit the revised draft to the Ministry of Federal Education for onward submission to the Federal Cabinet for approval. DPM/ FM while highlighting government’s commitment towards quality education stated that strengthening Pakistan’s higher education system and impartting knowledge through highest standards of quality, transparency, and excellence is the hallmark of this government. The Meeting was attended by Ministers for Law & Human Rights, IPC and Education and Professional Training, SAPM Tariq Bajwa, Federal Secretaries and relevant stakeholders.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, H.E. Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today met with Professor Emeritus Tan Sri Dr Zakri Abdul Hamid, Joint Chairman of the Malaysian Industry–Government Group for High Technology (MIGHT)/ Founding Director of International Institute of Science Diplomacy and Sustainability (IISDS-UCSI), on the sidelines of the 39th Asia-Pacific Roundtable, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The discussion centred on the way forward on Malaysia's proposal to establish an ASEAN Centre for Science Diplomacy (ACSD), aimed at advancing science-informed policymaking, strengthening capacity-building, and promoting knowledge exchange across ASEAN Member States. The meeting also underscored the importance of science diplomacy as a bridge for regional cooperation, in alignment with the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and the ASEAN Plan of Action on Science, Technology and Innovation (APASTI) 2026–2035. Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to harnessing science diplomacy as a strategic tool for regional resilience, sustainability, and inclusive development.

H.E. San Lwin, Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC), received a courtesy call from Ms. Phasporn Sangasubana, Executive Director of the ASEAN Centre for Sustainable Development Studies and Dialogue (ACSDSD), on 1 July 2026 at the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta. The meeting provided an opportunity to exchange views on regional sustainable development priorities and the implementation of the ASEAN Community Vision (ACV) 2045: Our Shared Future. Both sides discussed ACSDSD's ongoing work and future directions, as well as opportunities to strengthen collaboration in promoting sustainable development through research, dialogue, capacity building, knowledge sharing, and partnerships. The meeting also explored practical avenues for enhancing cooperation between the ASEAN Secretariat and ACSDSD in advancing ASEAN's sustainable development agenda, including fostering cross-sectoral collaboration, strengthening resilience, and supporting the effective implementation of the ASCC Strategic Plan. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to working together towards a more resilient, inclusive, sustainable, and people-centred ASEAN Community.

The Opening Ceremony of the 2nd Regional Forum on the ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC) Strategic Plan was convened on 1 July 2026 at the ASEAN Headquarters / ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta, Indonesia. The Forum, with the theme “Mainstreaming the ASCC Strategic Plan into Regional, National and Local Development Plans”, brings together Senior Officials Committee for the ASCC (SOCA), representatives from planning ministries of ASEAN Member States, ASEAN partners, think tanks and research organisations, civil society organisations, and various stakeholders to exchange views and approaches on mainstreaming the ASCC Strategic Plan into development plans, ensuring its sustained and effective implementation. The Opening Ceremony was also attended by the Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for the ASCC, Deputy Permanent Representative of the Permanent Mission of the Philippines to ASEAN, and Deputy Head of the Mission of Japan to ASEAN. In his welcome remarks, H.E. San Lwin, DSG of ASEAN for the ASCC, underscored the importance of the Forum in bridging the gap between policy development and implementation. He further highlighted that translating regional frameworks to concrete actions and initiatives is critical in delivering tangible benefits to the people of ASEAN. The 1st day of Forum also launched the Voices of the People of ASEAN: A Compendium of Stakeholder Insights for the ASCC Strategic Plan, which highlights the inclusive and participatory processes of the ASCC Strategic Plan development. The 2nd Regional Forum on the ASCC Strategic Plan, scheduled from 1 to 3 July 2026, was organised and hosted by the ASEAN Secretariat and SOCA Indonesia, with the support from the Government of Japan, through the Supporting the Development of the ASCC Strategic Plan project. #ASEAN #ASEANCommunity #ASCCStrategicPlan #ASCCPost2025 #JapanASEANIntegrationFund #JAIF #ACV2045
